S000171Brian's stack of Bernstein setsExample

Let X=ℝX = \mathbb{R} and let (Xi)i∈ω(X_i)_{i\in \omega} be a countably infinite partition of XX into Bernstein sets (for the Euclidean topology). Given x∈Xx \in X, let n∈ωn \in \omega be such that x∈Xnx \in X_n. Then basic open neighbourhoods of xx are given by the sets {x}∪(U∩⋃i<nXi)\{x\} \cup (U \cap \bigcup_{i<n}X_i), with UU (basic) open neighbourhood of xx in the Euclidean topology.

This topology is finer than Euclidean real numbers ℝ\mathbb R.

This space was constructed in Answer to "Example of an uncountable scattered space with some properties" by Will Brian, providing an example in ZFC for an uncountable, Hausdorff, first-countable, scattered, Lindelöf space.

S000175Radial planeExample

Let X=ℝ2X=\mathbb R^2 as a set. For the topology, a set U⊆XU\subseteq X is open if for every point x∈Ux\in U and line LL passing through xx, there is an open segment S⊆LS\subseteq L with x∈S⊆Ux\in S\subseteq U. In other words, UU is open in XX provided U∩LU\cap L is open in LL for each line LL with its Euclidean topology.

XX has a finer topology than Euclidean Plane ℝ2\mathbb R^2.

S000183KP Hart's non-sequentially discrete modified cocountable topologyExample

Let YY be Cocountable topology on ℝ\mathbb R and ZZ be Fort space on a countably infinite set. The space XX is the disjoint union Y∪ZY\cup Z with the minimal topology such that ZZ is a closed subspace of XX, and countable subsets of YY are all closed in XX.

  • Strongly KC
    Trait evidence · P000103

    Consider a countably compact subset A⊆XA\subseteq X. It must have finite intersection with the Cocountable topology on ℝ\mathbb R subspace YY, as otherwise it would contain an infinite closed discrete set. So A∩YA\cap Y is closed in XX.

    Since the Fort space on a countably infinite set subspace ZZ is closed in XX, the intersection A∩ZA\cap Z is closed in AA, hence countably compact. Since ZZ is Strongly KC, A∩ZA\cap Z is then closed in ZZ, and therefore closed in XX.

    Then AA is closed in XX as the union of two closed sets.

Let YY be a copy of One-point compactification of the sequential fan SωS_\omega. This space is X=(Y×ω)∪{∞}X=(Y\times\omega)\cup\{\infty\}. The subspace Y×ωY\times\omega is open with the product topology, and basic neighborhoods of ∞\infty are of the form (Y×(ω∖n))∪{∞}(Y\times(\omega\setminus n))\cup\{\infty\}.

S000191Dieudonné plankExample

The product space X=Y×ZX=Y\times Z where Y=[0,ω1]Y=[0,\omega_1] is given the topology with points of [0,ω1)[0,\omega_1) isolated and neighborhoods of ω1\omega_1 cocountable, and Z=[0,ω]Z=[0,\omega] is given the topology with points of [0,ω)[0,\omega) isolated and neighborhoods of ω\omega cofinite.

Equivalently, the product of Fortissimo space of size ℵ1\aleph_1 and Fort space on a countably infinite set.

The space XX has the same underlying set as Tychonoff plank, but with a finer topology.

Note that "Dieudonné plank" is also used to refer to Deleted Dieudonné plank.

S000192Modified telophase topologyExample

A refinement of the topology defined for Telophase topology. Let X=[0,∞)∪{∞E,∞D}X=[0,\infty)\cup\{\infty_E,\infty_D\}, E=2ℕ={2n:n∈ℕ}E=2\mathbb N=\{2n:n\in\mathbb N \}, and D=2ℕ+1={2n+1:n∈ℕ}D=2\mathbb N+1=\{2n+1:n\in\mathbb N\}. Then points of [0,∞)[0,\infty) have their usual neighborhoods (in the sense of Euclidean real numbers ℝ\mathbb R), ∞E\infty_E has basic neighborhoods of the form (a,∞)∖E(a,\infty)\setminus E, and ∞D\infty_D has basic neighborhoods of the form (a,∞)∖D(a,\infty)\setminus D.

  • Cozero complemented
    Trait evidence · P000061

    Any continuous function ff from XX to a Hausdorff space YY takes the same value at ∞E\infty_E and ∞D\infty_D, and thus factors through the quotient space X/{∞E,∞D}X/\{\infty_E,\infty_D\} that identifies the two infinity points. One can check that the quotient space is homeomorphic to the interval [0,+∞][0,+\infty] of the extended real line, and hence homeomorphic to Unit interval [0,1][0,1]. Since this space is T312T_{3 \frac{1}{2}}, it is the Tychonoff reflection of XX, with the quotient map φ\varphi as reflection map.

    The map φ\varphi is open at each point xx of the dense subset [0,∞)⊆X[0,\infty)\subseteq X (i.e., sends neighborhoods of xx to neighborhoods of f(x)f(x)). Since Unit interval [0,1][0,1] · Cozero complemented, the result then follows from the Remark after Proposition 2 in Cozero complemented property for a space and its Tychonoff reflection.

The long circle is the quotient space X=L/{m,M}X=L/\{m,M\} obtained by identifying mm and MM. Let q:L→Xq:L\to X denote the quotient map, and let p=q(m)=q(M)p=q(m)=q(M) be the identified point.

    Fix an element zz with m<z<Mm<z<M in LL. The interval [m,z][m,z] in LL is homeomorphic to the interval [0,1]⊆ℝ[0,1]\subseteq\mathbb R (see for example Answer to "Long ray - Proof of being locally Euclidean"). So there is a continuous function on [m,z][m,z] with f(m)=f(z)=0f(m)=f(z)=0 and f(x)>0f(x)>0 for m<x<zm<x<z. Extending this function to have value 00 outside of [m,z][m,z], one gets a continuous f:L→ℝf:L\to\mathbb R with common value 00 at mm and MM. Factoring ff via qq provides a continuous F:X→ℝF:X\to\mathbb R with corresponding cozero set U=coz(F)=(m,z)⊆XU=\text{coz}(F)=(m,z)\subseteq X. The function FF has constant value zero on q([z,M])q([z,M]).

    Claim: UU does not have a cozero complement in XX. Indeed, suppose V=coz(G)V=\text{coz}(G), with G:X→ℝG:X\to\mathbb R, is a cozero set disjoint from UU. Necessarily, G(p)=0G(p)=0 since p∈U‾p\in\overline U. The continuous function g=G∘q:L→ℝg=G\circ q:L\to\mathbb R satisfies g(M)=0g(M)=0. By the properties of Closed long ray, gg has constant value 00 on a whole interval [w,M][w,M] for some w<Mw<M in LL (see the "Related spaces" section of Answer to "Is the long ray cozero complemented?"). So GG has constant value zero on q([w,M])q([w,M]) and therefore U∪VU\cup V is not dense in XX.

S000201Infinite earringExample

The subspace of Euclidean Plane ℝ2\mathbb R^2 defined by

X=⋃n=1∞{(x,y)∈ℝ2:(x−1n)2+y2=(1n)2}\quad X=\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}\left\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2:\left(x-\frac{1}{n}\right)^2+y^2=\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)^2\right\}

that is, the union of circles of radius 1n\frac{1}{n} centered at (1n,0)(\frac{1}{n},0) for positive integers nn.

Not to be confused with Countable bouquet of circles, which has a finer topology.

Defined as "infinite earring" in section 71 of Topology (Munkres); usually known in the literature as "Hawaiian earring". Appears as Example 1.25 in Algebraic Topology (Hatcher) (available here) under the name "Shrinking wedge of circles"; however, note that it is not actually an example of a "wedge sum" as defined in e.g. wikipedia Wedge_sum or An Introduction to Algebraic Topology (Rotman).

S000205Warsaw circleExample

The set X={(x,sin⁡1x):x∈(0,1]}∪{(0,y):y∈[−2,1]}∪{(x,−2):x∈[0,1]}∪{(1,y):y∈[−2,sin⁡1]}X=\{(x, \sin\frac{1}{x}):x \in (0,1]\} \cup \{(0,y):y \in [-2,1]\} \cup \{(x,-2):x\in[0,1]\} \cup \{(1,y):y \in [-2,\sin 1]\} with the subspace topology inherited from ℝ2\mathbb{R}^2.

It consists of Closed Topologist's Sine Curve together with an extra arc joining its rightmost point to the point (0,−1)(0,-1). See Warsaw circle on Wikipedia or section 3 of Milnor–Thurston homology groups of the Warsaw Circle (J. Przewocki).

Note: There are a few closely related but non-isomorphic variants of the Warsaw circle (see the pictures in First Betti number of a Reeb graph is not greater than that of the space? for two of them). The description chosen here seems to be the most common.

S000207Cohen's modification of ω1×(ω1+1)\omega_1\times(\omega_1+1)Example

The product of Ordinal space ω1\omega_1 with Ordinal space ω1+1\omega_1+1, modified by declaring points of ω1×ω1\omega_1\times\omega_1 isolated. Each point ⟨α,ω1⟩\langle \alpha,\omega_1\rangle with α>0\alpha>0 has a local base consisting of the sets (β,α]×(γ,ω1](\beta,\alpha]\times(\gamma,\omega_1] for β<α\beta<\alpha and γ<ω1\gamma<\omega_1. The point ⟨0,ω1⟩\langle 0,\omega_1\rangle has a local base consisting of the sets {0}×(γ,ω1]\{0\}\times(\gamma,\omega_1] for γ<ω1\gamma<\omega_1. The resulting space XX has a finer topology than Product ω1×(ω1+1)\omega_1\times(\omega_1+1).

Each vertical slice {α}×[0,ω1]\{\alpha\}\times[0,\omega_1] for α<ω1\alpha<\omega_1 is homeomorphic to Fortissimo space of size ℵ1\aleph_1. Note however that XX is not homeomorphic to the product of Ordinal space ω1\omega_1 and Fortissimo space of size ℵ1\aleph_1.

H. J. Cohen provides this example, communicated by Bing, in Sur une problème de M. Dieudonné (H. J. Cohen) (http://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3186w/f290.image) to show that Strongly collectionwise normal is strictly stronger than Collectionwise normal. See Answer to "Is every $T_4$ topological space divisible?" for details in English.

S000209Circle with two originsExample

Choose a point 0∈S10 \in S^1 to be called the "origin", and replace 00 with two origins 010_1 and 020_2. Basic open neighborhoods of a point x≠0x \neq 0 are Euclidean open neighborhoods of xx not containing 00. Basic open neighborhoods of each origin 0i0_i are of the form (U∖{0})∪{0i}(U\setminus\{0\})\cup\{0_i\} with UU a Euclidean open neighborhood of 00.

Let {1,2}\{1, 2\} have the discrete topology. XX is homeomorphic to the quotient space of S1×{1,2}S^1 \times \{1, 2\} obtained by identifying ⟨θ,1⟩\langle \theta, 1 \rangle and ⟨θ,2⟩\langle \theta, 2 \rangle exactly when θ\theta is not the "origin" point.

XX is homeomorphic to the Alexandroff one-point compactification of Line with two origins.

S000213PseudocircleExample

Let XX be the complete bipartite poset K2,2K_{2,2}, with two incomparable elements in the bottom layer, two incomparable elements in the top layer, and every bottom element less than every top element.

Specifically, take X={0,1,2,3}X=\{0,1,2,3\} with bottom elements 0,20,2 and top elements 1,31,3. (The ordered pairs (a,b)(a,b) with a<ba<b are (0,1),(0,3),(2,1),(2,3)(0,1),(0,3),(2,1),(2,3).)

The topology on XX is the Alexandrov topology where the open sets are the upper sets of the poset: ∅,{1},{3},{1,3},{0,1,3},{2,1,3},X\varnothing, \{1\}, \{3\}, \{1,3\}, \{0,1,3\}, \{2,1,3\}, X.

This space can be viewed as the non-Hausdorff suspension of S0S^0 (Discrete topology on {0,1}\{0,1\}). See Definition 3.4.2 in Finite Spaces and Larger Contexts (J. P. May & E. Pishevar).

It is also homeomorphic to the quotient space of Circle S1S^1 obtained by identifying to a point each of the upper and lower open half circles. See Answer to "Is there a relationship between a quotient group of the fundamental group of X and the fundamental group of a quotient topology of X?".

See also https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/pseudocircle.

S000214Lexicographically ordered ℤω1\mathbb Z^{\omega_1}Example

The space X=ℤω1X = \mathbb Z ^ {\omega_1} with the order topology induced by lexicographic order. That is, for f,g∈Xf,g \in X we have f<gf < g if and only if there exists α∈ω1\alpha \in \omega_1 such that f(α)<g(α)f(\alpha) < g(\alpha) and f(β)=g(β)f(\beta) = g(\beta) for all β<α\beta < \alpha.

S000215Mysior planeExample

Let X=ℝ2X=\mathbb R^2 with each point (x,y)(x,y) with y≠0y\ne 0 isolated and each point (x,0)(x,0) having as local base the collection of open sets Un(x)U_n(x) (n=1,2,…n=1,2,\dots), where Un(x)U_n(x) is the union of the three line segments

  • {(x,y):−1/n<y<1/n}\{(x, y): -1/n < y < 1/n\},
  • {(x+1+y,y):0<y<1/n}\{(x+1+y, y): 0 < y < 1/n\},
  • {(x+2+y,−y):0<y<1/n}\{(x+\sqrt{2}+y, -y) : 0 < y < 1/n\}.

Introduced by Mysior in A union of realcompact spaces (Mysior). Also described in Example 5 of r-realcompact spaces (Bhattacharya & Dey).

S000217Left ray topology on ω1\omega_1Example

Let X=ω1X=\omega_1, with a base for the topology consisting of the left rays [0,α]=[0,α+1)[0,\alpha]=[0,\alpha+1) for α∈ω1\alpha\in\omega_1.

The open sets are the downward closed subsets of XX, which are XX, ∅\emptyset, the basic open sets above, and the rays [0,α)[0,\alpha) with α\alpha limit ordinal. This is the Alexandrov topology for the reverse ordering on ω1\omega_1.

S000220Right "closed-ray" topology on ω1\omega_1Example

As a set, X=ω1=[0,ω1)X=\omega_1=[0,\omega_1) with its usual order. The open sets are the upward-closed sets in the ordered set (X,≤)(X,\le), consisting of ∅\emptyset and the "closed rays" [α,→)[\alpha,\rightarrow) for α∈X\alpha\in X.

  • The open sets include the "open rays" since (β,→)=[β+1,→)(\beta,\rightarrow)=[\beta+1,\rightarrow).
  • The topology is the Alexandrov topology corresponding to (X,≤)(X,\le).

The closed sets are the downward-closed sets in (X,≤)(X,\le).

Compare with the coarser topology of Right "open-ray" topology on ω1\omega_1.

S000221Right "open-ray" topology on ω1\omega_1Example

As a set, X=ω1=[0,ω1)X=\omega_1=[0,\omega_1) with its usual order. The open sets for the topology are X,∅X,\emptyset and all "open rays" (α,→)=[α+1,→)(\alpha,\rightarrow)=[\alpha+1,\rightarrow) for α∈X\alpha\in X.

Note that the "closed rays" [β,→)[\beta,\rightarrow) with β\beta a limit ordinal are not open sets.

The nonempty proper closed sets are the intervals [0,α][0,\alpha] for α∈X.\alpha\in X.

Compare with the finer topology of Right "closed-ray" topology on ω1\omega_1.

Explicit traits supplied by Pi-Base; omitted traits have no assertion in this record.

  • ¬Injectively path connected
    Trait evidence · P000038

    Let f:[0,1]→Xf:[0,1]\to X be a path in XX. Take a countable dense subset EE of [0,1][0,1]. Its image f(E)f(E) is countable and thus bounded in XX, say by some u∈ω1u\in\omega_1. So f(E)f(E) is contained in the closed set [0,u][0,u]. And by density of EE in [0,1][0,1], f([0,1])f([0,1]) is also contained in [0,u][0,u]. Since [0,u][0,u] is countable, ff cannot be injective.

    Pinned trait record
  • Fixed point property
    Trait evidence · P000089

    The specialization preorder on XX corresponds to the natural order of ordinals (α∈{β}‾  ⟺  α≤β\alpha\in\overline{\{\beta\}}\iff\alpha\le\beta). Since continuous functions preserve the specialization preorder, any continuous f:X→Xf:X\to X is monotone non-decreasing (α≤β  ⟹  f(α)≤f(β)\alpha\le\beta\implies f(\alpha)\le f(\beta)).

    Now let α0=0\alpha_0=0 and αn=f(αn−1)\alpha_n=f(\alpha_{n-1}) for n=1,2,…n=1,2,\dots. This defines a non-decreasing sequence α0≤α1≤⋯\alpha_0\le \alpha_1\le \cdots in ω1\omega_1. Let αω:=sup⁡nαn∈X\alpha_\omega:=\sup_n \alpha_n\in X. For each nn we have αn≤αω\alpha_n\le\alpha_\omega, and hence αn+1=f(αn)≤f(αω)\alpha_{n+1}=f(\alpha_n)\le f(\alpha_\omega). Consequently, αω≤f(αω)\alpha_\omega\le f(\alpha_\omega). On the other hand, αω\alpha_\omega belongs to the closure of {αn:n∈ω}\{\alpha_n:n\in\omega\}. By continuity, f(αω)f(\alpha_\omega) belongs to the closure of {αn+1:n∈ω}\{\alpha_{n+1}:n\in\omega\}. So f(αω)f(\alpha_\omega) cannot be strictly larger than αω\alpha_\omega. This proves that f(αω)=αωf(\alpha_\omega)=\alpha_\omega.

    Pinned trait record

  • ¬Toronto
    Trait evidence · P000219

    Let YY denote the subspace of successor cardinals in XX, that is, Y={β+1:β∈ω1}Y=\{\beta+1:\beta\in\omega_1\}. Note that ∣Y∣=∣X∣|Y|=|X|.

    Because ω1\omega_1 is an initial ordinal, (Y,≤)(Y,\le) is order-isomorphic to (ω1,≤)(\omega_1,\le). And since an element α=β+1∈Y\alpha=\beta+1\in Y has [α,→)=(β,→)[\alpha,\to)=(\beta,\to) as smallest neighborhood in XX, it has [α,→)∩Y[\alpha,\to)\cap Y as smallest neighborhood in YY. This shows that the subspace topology on YY is homeomorphic to Right "closed-ray" topology on ω1\omega_1.

    But Right "closed-ray" topology on ω1\omega_1 is not homeomorphic to Right "open-ray" topology on ω1\omega_1, for example because only the first one is Alexandrov.

S000223Ellentuck topology on [ω]ω[\omega]^\omegaExample

Let X=[ω]ωX = [\omega]^\omega, the set of infinite sets of nonnegative integers, and give it the topology with basis consisting of all sets

[s,A]={B∈X:s⊆B⊆s∪A   and   max⁡(s)<min⁡(B∖s)}[s, A] = \{B \in X: s \subseteq B \subseteq s \cup A \;\text{ and }\; \max(s) < \min(B \setminus s)\}

for a finite s⊆ωs\subseteq\omega and an infinite A⊆ωA\subseteq\omega. If s=∅s = \emptyset we let max⁡(s)=−1\max(s) = -1.

Note: Omitting the condition max⁡(s)<min⁡(B∖s)\max(s) < \min(B \setminus s) would give another base for the same topology, but the form chosen above is usually more convenient.

Introduced by Ellentuck in A new proof that analytic sets are Ramsey (E. Ellentuck) (https://www.jstor.org/stable/2272356). See also Definition 26.25 in Set theory (T. Jech, 2003) and the section "The Ellentuck Topology" on p. 248 of Combinatorial set theory (L. Halbeisen, 2017)

Sources cited by Pi-Base

  • A new proof that analytic sets are Ramsey (E. Ellentuck)
  • Set theory (T. Jech, 2003)
  • Combinatorial set theory (L. Halbeisen, 2017)

The subspace ℝ+2={(x,y)∈ℝ2:y≥0}\mathbb R^2_+=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2 : y\ge 0\} of Euclidean Plane ℝ2\mathbb R^2.

This space is homemorphic to the product of Euclidean real numbers ℝ\mathbb R and Interval [0,1)[0,1).

Explicit traits supplied by Pi-Base; omitted traits have no assertion in this record.

  • ¬Compact
    Trait evidence · P000016

    XX is not a bounded subset of ℝ2\mathbb R^2.

    Pinned trait record
  • ¬Fixed point property
    Trait evidence · P000089

    The map (x,y)↦(x+1,y)(x,y)\mapsto (x+1,y) has no fixed point.

    Pinned trait record
  • ¬Locally orderable
    Trait evidence · P000120

    XX contains an open subspace homeomorphic to Euclidean Plane ℝ2\mathbb R^2 and S000176 · P000120.

    Pinned trait record
  • ¬Locally Euclidean
    Trait evidence · P000122

    The point (0,0)∈X(0,0)\in X does not have a neighborhood homeomorphic to some ℝn\mathbb R^n.

    Pinned trait record
  • Embeddable into Euclidean space
    Trait evidence · P000184

    By definition.

    Pinned trait record
  • Contractible
    Trait evidence · P000199

    Since XX is a convex subset of ℝ2\mathbb R^2, it can be deformation retracted to a point using a straight-line homotopy.

  • ¬Has a cut point
    Trait evidence · P000204

    XX is the product of two connected spaces, each with at least two points. Such a product minus a point is always connected (see $(X\times Y)\setminus (A\times B)$ is connected for $A,B$ proper subsets of connected $X,Y$).

    Sources cited by Pi-Base

    XX satisfies Locally an nn-Euclidean half-space with n=2n=2.

    Pinned trait record

S000226Fortissimo space of size ℵ1\aleph_1 and Sierpinski space glued at their limit pointsExample

Let XX be a set of cardinality ℵ1\aleph_1 with two distinguished points p,q∈Xp,q\in X. Every point x≠px\ne p is isolated and the open neighborhoods of pp are the cocountable subsets of XX containing both pp and qq.

Two subspaces are worth noting:

  • Y=X∖{q}Y=X\setminus\{q\} is homeomorphic to Fortissimo space of size ℵ1\aleph_1 with pp as limit point;
  • Z={p,q}Z=\{p,q\} is homeomorphic to Sierpinski space with pp as limit point.

XX could also be described as the result of "gluing" Fortissimo space of size ℵ1\aleph_1 and Sierpinski space at their limit points; that is, XX is homeomorphic to the quotient of the topological sum of these two spaces with their limit points identified.

Explicit traits supplied by Pi-Base; omitted traits have no assertion in this record.

  • ¬T1T_1
    Trait evidence · P000002

    Sierpinski space embeds into XX and Sierpinski space · T1T_1.

    Pinned trait record
  • Lindelöf
    Trait evidence · P000018

    Let 𝒰\mathscr U be an open cover of XX. There is a countable 𝒱⊆𝒰\mathscr V\subseteq\mathscr U with Y⊆⋃𝒱Y\subseteq\bigcup\mathscr V because Fortissimo space of size ℵ1\aleph_1 · Lindelöf. Since every neighborhood of pp contains ZZ, 𝒱\mathscr V is also a cover of XX.

    Pinned trait record
  • ¬Weakly countably compact
    Trait evidence · P000021

    YY is a closed subspace of XX and Fortissimo space of size ℵ1\aleph_1 · Weakly countably compact.

    Pinned trait record
  • Cardinality =ℵ1=\aleph_1
    Trait evidence · P000114

    By construction.

  • Anticompact
    Trait evidence · P000136

    The subspace YY is closed in XX and anticompact (Fortissimo space of size ℵ1\aleph_1 · Anticompact). So every compact subset of XX intersects YY in a finite set, and is itself finite.

    Pinned trait record
  • P-space
    Trait evidence · P000147

    The neighborhoods of pp in XX are the sets V∪ZV\cup Z with VV neighborhood of pp in YY. Since S000155 · P000147, pp is also a P-point in XX. And every other (isolated) point is trivially a P-point.

    Pinned trait record
  • Well-based
    Trait evidence · P000174

    The neighborhoods of pp in XX are the sets V∪ZV\cup Z with VV neighborhood of pp in YY. Since S000155 · P000174, there is a neighborhood base 𝒩\mathscr N for pp in YY that is totally ordered by inclusion. Then {V∪Z:V∈𝒩}\{V\cup Z:V\in\mathscr N\} is a totally ordered neighborhood base for pp in XX. And XX is trivially well-based at each of the other (isolated) points.

    Pinned trait record
  • Almost discrete
    Trait evidence · P000203

    All points except pp are isolated.

    Pinned trait record
  • Semilocally simply connected
    Trait evidence · P000229

    The path components of XX are ZZ and the singletons {x}\{x\} with x∈Y∖{p}x\in Y\setminus\{p\} (because Sierpinski space · Path connected and every {x}\{x\} with x∈Y∖{p}x\in Y\setminus\{p\} is clopen in XX).

    And since Sierpinski space · Semilocally simply connected, every path component of XX is Semilocally simply connected.

    Pinned trait record
  • ¬Has open connected components
    Trait evidence · P000234

    Every neighborhood VV of pp contains a point x∈Y∖{p}x\in Y\setminus\{p\}. Hence VV is not connected since {x}\{x\} is clopen in XX.

    Pinned trait record

S000227Product ℝ×ω\mathbb{R}\times\omegaExample

X=ℝ×ωX=\mathbb{R} \times \omega is the product of Euclidean real numbers ℝ\mathbb R and Discrete topology on ω\omega.

This space is homeomorphic to the disjoint union ⨆i=0∞ℝ\bigsqcup_{i=0}^\infty \mathbb{R} of a countably infinite number of copies of Euclidean real numbers ℝ\mathbb R.

S000228Wheel with detached spokesExample

The subspace X=⋃n=0∞AnX=\bigcup_{n=0}^\infty A_n of Euclidean Plane ℝ2\mathbb R^2, where An={tpn:t∈[2−n,1]}A_n=\{ t p_n: t\in [2^{-n},1] \} for n≥1n\geq 1, A0={(0,0)}A_0= \{(0,0)\} and {pn}n=1∞\{p_n\}_{n=1}^\infty is a countable dense set in the unit circle in ℝ2\mathbb R^2 (Circle S1S^1 · Separable).

Explicit traits supplied by Pi-Base; omitted traits have no assertion in this record.

  • σ\sigma-compact
    Trait evidence · P000017

    XX is the countable union of the compact sets AnA_n (homeomorphic to Unit interval [0,1][0,1] or The Singleton).

    Pinned trait record
  • Connected
    Trait evidence · P000036

    Suppose U⊆XU\subseteq X is a clopen set and (0,0)∈U(0,0)\in U. Since each AnA_n is Connected, it has to be contained either in UU or X∖UX\setminus U. Observe that all but finitely many spokes AnA_n intersect UU (a neighbourhood of (0,0)(0,0)), therefore they are contained in UU. Then UU is a dense subset of XX (it is dense in the unit disc) and consequently U=XU=X. Hence the space XX does not admit nontrivial clopen set and is Connected.

    Pinned trait record
  • ¬Locally connected
    Trait evidence · P000041

    The connected components of the open set X∖{(0,0)}X\setminus\{(0,0)\} are precisely the AnA_n's for n≥1n\geq 1. They are not open, hence XX is not locally connected.

    Pinned trait record
  • ¬Totally path disconnected
    Trait evidence · P000046

    Each of the sets AnA_n for n≥1n\geq 1 is homeomorphic to Unit interval [0,1][0,1].

    Pinned trait record
  • Meager
    Trait evidence · P000056

    Each of the sets AnA_n is nowhere dense, because it is nowhere dense in the unit disc in which XX is dense.

    Pinned trait record
  • Embeddable into Euclidean space
    Trait evidence · P000184

    XX is defined as a subspace of Euclidean Plane ℝ2\mathbb R^2.

    Pinned trait record
  • ¬σ\sigma-connected
    Trait evidence · P000189

    By construction, XX is a countable union of pairwise disjoint closed (compact) sets AnA_n, n≥0n\geq 0.

    Pinned trait record
  • Has a cut point
    Trait evidence · P000204

    S000228 · P000036, but X1=X∖{(0,0)}X_1=X\setminus \{(0,0)\} is not connected for there exists a line LL passing through (0,0)(0,0) disjoint from X1X_1 (there are only countably many such lines that intersect X1X_1).

    Pinned trait record
  • ¬Cut point space
    Trait evidence · P000205

    It is evident that X∖{pn}X\setminus\{p_n\} (n≥1n\geq 1) is Connected for the same reason that S000228 · P000036.

    Pinned trait record
